label: def:dcd
title: Definition
head: environment
name: Delay Complexity Dimension

label: prop:limits
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:limits}
(i) If $q(W)=1$, then $\eta(W)=1$ and $\mathrm{DCD}=d$, recovering
classical VC. (ii) If $D\perp Y\mid X$, then $I^0_W=0$,
$\eta(W)=q(W)$, and $\mathrm{DCD}=d/q(W)$, recovering censored
ERM~\citep{ausset2022empirical} in the binary setting.
(iii) If $H(Y\mid X,A{=}0)=0$ wherever censoring has positive
probability (the censoring event determines the label), then
$\eta(W)=1$ and $\mathrm{DCD}=d$ regardless of $q(W)$. The delay is
then maximally informative.
head: environment
name: Limiting cases

title: Proof
body_md:
All three cases follow from \eqref{eq:identity}. The censored
residual term is multiplied by $1-q=0$ in case (i). It equals
$H(Y\mid X)$ in case (ii). It equals $0$ in case (iii).
head: environment

label: rem:fano
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:fano}
The $\mathrm{DCD}$ is a distribution-dependent quantity; the
shattered-set size never exceeds $d$, and what scales as $d/\eta(W)$
is the sample complexity of the constructed instances. The proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:dcd-lb} exhibits $2^{\Omega(d)}$
$\varepsilon$-risk-separated hypotheses whose observation laws
differ by at most $C\varepsilon^2\eta(W)$ in per-sample KL, forcing
$\Theta(\mathrm{DCD}/\varepsilon^2)$ samples.
head: environment
name: Local Fano characterization

label: thm:dcd-lb
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:dcd-lb}
For every $q\in(0,1]$ and every censored-branch information ratio
$\iota\in[0,\iota_{\max}(q)]$ realizable by a delay channel at
balanced labels, there is a distribution $P$ with $q(W)=q$ and
$I^0_W/H(Y\mid X)=\iota$, so that $\eta(W)=q+(1-q)\iota$ and
$\mathrm{DCD}=d/\eta(W)$. Under $P$, any
$(\varepsilon,\delta)$-PAC learner needs
\[
n\;\ge\;c\,\frac{d+\log(1/\delta)}{\eta(W)\,\varepsilon^2}
\;=\;\Omega\!\bigl((\mathrm{DCD}+\log(1/\delta))/\varepsilon^2\bigr).
\]
head: environment
name: Information-theoretic lower bound

title: Proof
body_md:
Varshamov--Gilbert gives a packing $\Sigma\subseteq\{0,1\}^d$ of size
$\ge 2^{d/8}$ with pairwise Hamming distance $\ge d/4$. For each
$\sigma\in\Sigma$ define $P_\sigma$ with
$\mathbb{P}(Y=1\mid X=x_i)=\tfrac12+\varepsilon(2\sigma_i-1)$ on a
VC-shattered set. The delay channel
$a_y=\mathbb{P}(D\le W\mid Y{=}y,x_i)$ is held fixed across $\sigma$. Write
$\bar a=(a_1+a_0)/2$ and $\gamma_W=a_0-a_1$. The censoring
probability $\mathbb{P}_\sigma(A=0\mid x_i)=1-\bar a+\varepsilon\gamma_W$
itself depends on $\sigma_i$. The observation must therefore be
treated as a single three-outcome law,
$(A,YA)\in\{(1,1),(1,0),(0,0)\}$ with probabilities
$\bigl((\tfrac12+\varepsilon)a_1,\,(\tfrac12-\varepsilon)a_0,\,
1-\bar a+\varepsilon\gamma_W\bigr)$.
The exact three-term $\chi^2$ computation, the bound
$|\gamma_W|\le 2\min\{\bar a,1-\bar a\}$, and the entropy sandwich
$2s^2\le\ln 2-H_2(\tfrac12+s)\le 4s^2$ applied to the censored
posterior $\tfrac12+s$, $s=\gamma_W/(4(1-\bar a))$, give for
$\varepsilon\le 1/8$
\[
\mathrm{KL}_i(P_\sigma\|P_{\sigma'})\le
C\,\varepsilon^2\Bigl[\bar a(x_i)+\bigl(1-\bar a(x_i)\bigr)
\tfrac{I^0(x_i)}{H(Y\mid X)}\Bigr],\quad C\le 34.
\]
By \eqref{eq:identity}, the bracket averages over the design exactly
to $\eta(W)$. The joint KL of $n$ samples is therefore at most
$C n\varepsilon^2\eta(W)$. Fano then yields the $d$-term. The same
construction on a single point with the two-point
Bretagnolle--Huber bound \citep{tsybakov2009introduction} yields the
$\log(1/\delta)$-term. Sweeping $(a_1,a_0)$ at fixed mean $q$
realizes every $\iota\in[0,\iota_{\max}(q)]$. The full
computation appears in the full version.
head: environment
name: Proof sketch

label: rem:balanced
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:balanced}
Within the construction ($p=\tfrac12$), the censored-branch ratio
$\iota(x)=I^0(x)/H(Y\mid x)$ at each point obeys
$\iota(x)\le 4s(x)^2/\ln 2$. The bound
$|\gamma_W|\le 2\min\{\bar a,1-\bar a\}$ then gives
$(1-\bar a)\,\iota(x)\le \bar a/\ln 2$ pointwise. Therefore
\[
\eta(W)\;\le\;\Bigl(1+\frac{1}{\ln 2}\Bigr)\,q(W)\;\le\;2.5\,q(W)
\]
for every delay channel with balanced labels. Coverage far
exceeding $q(W)$ is an unbalanced-label phenomenon
(Remark~\ref{rem:tightness}).
head: environment
name: Achievable coverage at balanced labels

label: ass:oracle
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:oracle}
The learner has access to the calibrated posterior
$\hat Y(x,a)=\mathbb{E}[Y\mid X{=}x,A{=}a]$, and in
Section~\ref{sec:informative} to its quantized version
$\hat Y(x,q)=\mathbb{E}[Y\mid X{=}x,Q_M{=}q]$. The label is unobserved
exactly when $A=0$, so this posterior is an oracle quantity;
estimating it from censored data is discussed in
Remark~\ref{rem:plugin} and open.
head: environment
name: Oracle pseudo-label posterior

label: thm:dcd-ub
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:dcd-ub}
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:oracle}, pseudo-label ERM returns $\hat h$
with
\[
R(\hat h)-\inf_{h\in\mathcal{H}}R(h)
\le C\sqrt{\tfrac{d/q(W)+\log(1/\delta)}{n}}
\]
up to logarithmic factors, with probability at least $1-\delta$.
head: environment
name: Oracle pseudo-label ERM upper bound

title: Proof
body_md:
Construct pseudo-labels $\hat Y(x,a)=\mathbb{E}[Y\mid X=x,A=a]$
(Assumption~\ref{ass:oracle}). Run ERM on
the lifted class $\mathcal{H}'=\{(x,a)\mapsto h(x)\}$ with the calibrated
square-loss surrogate. The bias-variance decomposition
(Lemma~\ref{lem:biasvar}, stated with the other supporting lemmas in
Section~\ref{sec:informative}) shows that the residual variance is at
most $H(Y\mid X)-I_W$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:quantize}, via data processing).
Lemma~\ref{lem:rad} controls the lifted-class Rademacher
complexity at $O(\sqrt{d/n})$. The two combine, via the Massart-noise
calibration of \citet{massart2006risk} and the $1/q(W)$ censoring
factor of the lifted-class step, to $O(\sqrt{d/(n q(W))})$. The
constants are tracked in the full version.
head: environment
name: Proof sketch

label: rem:tightness
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:tightness}
Under unbalanced label priors, $\eta(W)$ can far exceed $q(W)$ (the
heavily censored, informative regime), and there the upper bound is
within a factor $\eta(W)/q(W)$ of the lower bound. The
calibrated pseudo-label $\hat Y(X,A)$ is locally Fisher-efficient. Its
per-sample Fisher information matches the $\chi^2$ rate charged by the
lower bound. We therefore conjecture that the
$O(\sqrt{\mathrm{DCD}/n})$ rate holds in this regime as well. A
variance-weighted uniform-convergence argument would settle it, and
we leave this open (Section~\ref{sec:discussion}).
head: environment
name: Tightness in the remaining regime

label: lem:quantize
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Quantization preserves information

title: Proof
body_md:
Take any quantizer whose partition refines the in-window indicator
(the successive-refinement construction on the posterior is one such
choice). Then $A$ is a deterministic function of $Q_M=f_M(D\wedge W)$,
and data processing gives
$I(Y;Q_M\mid X)\ge I(Y;A\mid X)=I_W$.
Refining further only increases $I(Y;Q_M\mid X)$ toward
$I(Y;D\wedge W\mid X)$.
head: environment

label: lem:biasvar
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:biasvar}
For $Q_M=f_M(D\wedge W)$ and $\hat Y(x,q)=\mathbb{E}[Y\mid X=x,Q_M=q]$,
$\mathbb{E}[(h(X)-Y)^2]=\mathbb{E}[(h(X)-\hat Y(X,Q_M))^2]+\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{Var}(Y\mid X,Q_M)]$,
and $\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{Var}(Y\mid X,Q_M)]\le H(Y\mid X)-I(Y;Q_M\mid X)$.
head: environment
name: Bias-variance decomposition

title: Proof
body_md:
The cross term vanishes by the tower property, since
$\hat Y(X,Q_M)=\mathbb{E}[Y\mid X,Q_M]$. For the entropy bound,
$\mathrm{Var}(Y\mid X,Q_M)=\rho(1-\rho)\le H_2(\rho)$ with
$\rho=\mathbb{P}(Y{=}1\mid X,Q_M)$. Taking expectations and using
$H(Y\mid X,Q_M)=H(Y\mid X)-I(Y;Q_M\mid X)$ gives the claim.
head: environment

label: lem:rad
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:rad}
The lifted class $\mathcal{H}'=\{(x,q)\mapsto h(x)\}$ satisfies
$\mathrm{VC}(\mathcal{H}')=d$, and its empirical Rademacher complexity is
$O(\sqrt{d/n})$. Neither quantity depends on $M$.
head: environment
name: Lifted-class complexity

title: Proof
body_md:
Members of $\mathcal{H}'$ ignore the bin argument. A set of pairs
$\{(x_i,q_i)\}$ containing a repeated $x_i$ cannot be shattered, and
a set with distinct $x_i$ is shattered by $\mathcal{H}'$ exactly when
$\{x_i\}$ is shattered by $\mathcal{H}$. Hence
$\mathrm{VC}(\mathcal{H}')=\mathrm{VC}(\mathcal{H})=d$. Sauer--Shelah with
symmetrization (\citealt{devroye1996probabilistic}) yields the
Rademacher bound.
head: environment

label: thm:info-tradeoff
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Quantized oracle pseudo-label ERM

label: thm:neff
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:neff}
With the indicator quantizer ($M=2$), oracle pseudo-label ERM
achieves excess risk $C\sqrt{(d/q(W)+\log(1/\delta))/n}$ up to
logarithmic factors, the $M=2$ case of
Theorem~\ref{thm:info-tradeoff} and the bound of
Theorem~\ref{thm:dcd-ub}. The variance-dependent term improves by
the factor $1-I_W/H(Y\mid X)$. Equivalently, the effective sample
size is $n_{\mathrm{eff}}=c\,n\,q(W)$. Informative delay never
degrades the guarantee. It reduces the residual label variance.
head: environment
name: Effective sample size

title: Proof
body_md:
Lemma~\ref{lem:biasvar} splits the calibrated square-loss risk into
approximation plus residual variance. Lemma~\ref{lem:rad} bounds the
uniform deviations by $C\sqrt{d/n}$ for every $M$, since the lifted
class ignores the bin. The Massart calibration of
\citet{massart2006risk} converts variance into rate, and the $1/q(W)$
censoring factor enters through the lifted-class step, exactly as in
Theorem~\ref{thm:dcd-ub}. For Theorem~\ref{thm:neff}, take $M=2$. The
residual variance is then at most $H(Y\mid X)-I_W$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:quantize}. Finer bins retain more information and
leave the complexity term unchanged, so in the oracle setting the
bound is monotone in $M$; the tradeoff that finer bins do create is
in calibration (Remark~\ref{rem:plugin}).
head: environment

label: rem:plugin
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:plugin}
The guarantees above assume the calibrated posterior
$\hat Y(x,q)=\mathbb{E}[Y\mid X{=}x,Q_M{=}q]$ (Assumption~\ref{ass:oracle}).
With an estimate $\tilde Y$ in
its place, the two square-loss risks differ by at most
$2\,\mathbb{E}|\tilde Y-\hat Y|$ for $h,\hat Y,\tilde Y\in[0,1]$, so every
bound in this section degrades additively by
$O(\mathbb{E}|\tilde Y-\hat Y|)$. This additive term carries the cost of
quantization: $M$ bin posteriors must be calibrated from the
same $n$ samples, so $\mathbb{E}|\tilde Y-\hat Y|$ generically grows with
$M$, and an information versus calibration tradeoff appears in the
estimated setting even though the oracle bound of
Theorem~\ref{thm:info-tradeoff} is monotone. A bin-indexed class
$\{(x,q)\mapsto h_q(x)\}$ would reinstate a complexity term of order
$dM$; we do not take that route, since no bin is available at
prediction time. Estimating $\hat Y$ requires a model of the
delay channel, because $Y$ is unobserved exactly when $A=0$.
Identifiability conditions and rates for this calibration step are
open (Section~\ref{sec:discussion}).
head: environment
name: Estimated pseudo-labels and the cost of bins

label: thm:expedition
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:expedition}
Let the $B$ expedited examples be drawn uniformly at random from the
$n$, independently of the observations. Under
Assumption~\ref{ass:oracle} there is a learner achieving
\[
R(\hat h)-\inf_{h\in\mathcal{H}}R(h)\le C\sqrt{\tfrac{d}{n q(W)+B}+\tfrac{\log(1/\delta)}{n}}.
\]
head: environment
name: Effective sample size with random expedition

title: Proof
body_md:
A uniform subsample of an i.i.d.\ sample is i.i.d., so the expedited
stream consists of $B$ fully labeled draws from the original input
distribution, and the passive stream contributes effective sample
size $n\,q(W)$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:neff}. Bernstein-type
concentration on the union of the two streams
(\citealt{devroye1996probabilistic}, Ch.~12) gives the
$\sqrt{d/(n\,q(W)+B)}$ term.
head: environment
name: Proof sketch

label: thm:policy
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:policy}
Let $\Delta(x)=\mathbb{P}_{h\sim\mu_V}(h(x)=1)\,\mathbb{P}_{h\sim\mu_V}(h(x)=0)$
be the disagreement at $x$ under $\mu_V$. Consider choosing a batch
of at most $B$ expedition points, fixed before any expedited label is
revealed, to maximize the expected reduction of the $\mu$-mass of the
version space. The objective is monotone and submodular, greedy
selection achieves a $(1-1/e)$ approximation to the best fixed batch,
and the greedy marginal gain factors as
$\Delta(x)\cdot\mathbb{P}(D>W\mid x)$. The threshold rule
$\pi^\star(x)=\mathbf{1}\{\Delta(x)\mathbb{P}(D>W\mid x)\ge\tau\}$, with
$\tau$ chosen to spend the budget $B$, implements the greedy batch.
head: environment
name: Threshold policy

title: Proof
body_md:
The expected-mass-reduction objective is monotone, since queries only
exclude hypotheses. It is submodular over fixed batches, since the
conditional information gain of a query is non-increasing in the
already-selected set by the chain rule. Greedy maximization under a
cardinality budget therefore achieves $(1-1/e)$ of the best fixed
batch \citep{nemhauser1978analysis}. \citet{shaeiri2026pac} use
analogous arguments. The greedy marginal gain factors as
$\Delta(x)\cdot\mathbb{P}(D>W\mid x)$, and the threshold form is its
Lagrangian dual at budget $B$. Details appear in the full version.
head: environment
name: Proof sketch

label: rem:scope
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:scope}
Theorems~\ref{thm:expedition} and~\ref{thm:policy} answer different
questions: sample-size accounting for i.i.d.\ expedited draws, and
an approximation guarantee for the version-space objective with a
batch fixed in advance. The threshold policy's picks concentrate
where $\Delta(x)\mathbb{P}(D>W\mid x)$ is large, so they are neither
distributed as $P_X$ nor, in sequential variants that update $V$
between picks, independent, and Theorem~\ref{thm:expedition} does
not apply to them as stated. Extending it requires importance
weighting for the induced covariate shift and martingale
concentration for adaptive selection, and converting
version-space-mass reduction into excess risk requires additional
structure. Both extensions are open (Section~\ref{sec:discussion}).
Experiment~3 evaluates the threshold policy directly.
head: environment
name: Scope of the two guarantees

label: rem:surrogate
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:surrogate}
Exact version-space maintenance is intractable in high dimension, and
the experiments estimate $\Delta(x)$ with a pilot model
(Section~\ref{sec:experiments}). The greedy induction tolerates this.
If every step selects a point whose marginal gain is within $\zeta$
of the best available, the batch attains $(1-1/e)$ of the optimal
fixed-batch value minus a term of order $B\zeta$, and a
$\zeta$-accurate pilot inherits Theorem~\ref{thm:policy} up to that
term.
head: environment
name: Practical surrogate

label: ass:maturation
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:maturation}
Sample size scales as $n(W)=n(1-W/T)$ for $W<T$. The label observed
at delay $W$ has Bernoulli flip rate
$\nu(W)=\nu_0 e^{-\beta W}$ with $\beta>0$,
$\nu_0\in(0,\tfrac12)$.
head: environment
name: Maturation noise with horizon

label: thm:nonzero-delay-optimal
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:nonzero-delay-optimal}
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:maturation}, the excess risk $\Phi(W)$ of
pseudo-label ERM trained at window $W$ satisfies
$\Phi(W)\le C_1\nu_0^2 e^{-2\beta W}+C_2 d/[n(1-W/T)]$. There is an
open subset of $(\beta,\nu_0,n,T,d)$ for which the minimizer
$W^\star$ lies in $(0,T)$ and $\Phi(W^\star)<\Phi(0)$.
head: environment
name: Nonzero delay strictly improves

title: Proof
body_md:
The bias term is the squared-loss propagation of the flip rate. The
variance term is the censored sample size from
Theorem~\ref{thm:dcd-ub}. The condition
$\Phi'(0)<0$ requires $2\beta C_1\nu_0^2>C_2 d/(Tn)$, which holds for
large enough $\beta$, $\nu_0$, and $n$. Since $\Phi(W)\to\infty$ as
$W\to T^-$, the minimizer is then interior.
head: environment
name: Proof sketch

label: thm:diversity
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:diversity}
Suppose each labeler contributes $n$ draws, so that
$\hat h_{\mathrm{mix}}$, which combines the $K$ labelers'
pseudo-label estimates with inverse-variance weights
$w_k\propto\eta_k$, trains on $nK$ examples, while
$\hat h_{\mathrm{best}}$, which uses only the single best labeler,
trains on $n$. Then
$\mathbb{E}[R(\hat h_{\mathrm{mix}})]\le
\mathbb{E}[R(\hat h_{\mathrm{best}})]\cdot\eta_{\max}/(\bar\eta(1+H_e(\{w_k\})))$,
where $H_e$ is the entropy of the weights.
head: environment
name: Diversity benefit under per-labeler normalization

title: Proof
body_md:
Labeler $k$'s pseudo-label estimate has variance $O(1/(n\eta_k))$.
The inverse-variance mixture has variance
$O(1/(n\sum_k\eta_k))=O(1/(nK\bar\eta))$. The best single labeler has
variance $O(1/(n\eta_{\max}))$. Translating standard deviations to
excess risk and applying a Jensen correction for the effective number
of labelers yields the entropy factor $1+H_e(\{w_k\})$. The Jensen
step is carried out in the full version.
head: environment
name: Proof sketch

label: thm:phase
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:phase}
Let $\Lambda=n\,q(W)+B$, $\Lambda_0=n\,\eta(W)+B$, $d=\mathrm{VC}(\mathcal{H})$.
(i) If $\Lambda_0=o(d)$, no consistent learner exists, and the
excess risk is $\Omega(1)$. (ii) If $\Lambda=\omega(d)$, the excess
risk is $O(\sqrt{d/\Lambda})=o(1)$; when $\Lambda=\Theta(n)$ this is
the $n^{-1/2}$ rate. (iii) If $\Lambda=\Omega(d\log n)$, the
local-Rademacher rate $\sqrt{d\log n/\Lambda}$ applies.
head: environment
name: Phase regimes

title: Proof
body_md:
Case (i) is Theorem~\ref{thm:dcd-lb} in the limit $\Lambda_0/d\to 0$.
The impossibility threshold is governed by $\eta(W)$, and the
achievable threshold by $q(W)$. Case (ii) is
Theorem~\ref{thm:expedition}, whose bound is $o(1)$ exactly when
$d/\Lambda\to 0$. Case (iii) is the standard
local-Rademacher refinement under bounded variance
(\citealt{devroye1996probabilistic}), with $\Lambda$ in place of $n$.
Experiment~6 probes all three regimes.
head: environment
name: Proof sketch
